"PREMIER PLAY" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of its unclaimed prize money, most is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

The most common prize left on "PREMIER PLAY" right now is $100.

Everything above about "PREMIER PLAY" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2414.headline: Where the prize money is

2415.body:
"Double The Money" is in the middle of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

Everything above about "Double The Money" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2415.headline: How far along this game is

2416.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Loaded with $2,000s", about a third are still unsold. The game is well into its run, with 1,129 of 3,372 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

If you play "Loaded with $2,000s" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2416.headline: Where this game is in its run

2419.body:
"Bronze 7s" is well into its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Every line of Bronze 7s's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
2419.headline: How far along this game is

2420.body:
"Silver 7s" has two of three top prizes left and is near the midpoint of its run. About half of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Today's free summary of "Silver 7s" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
2420.headline: Tickets sold so far

2421.body:
"Gold 7s" has gone three weeks without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a third of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $577,777 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

If "Gold 7s" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
2421.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

2422.body:
The key fact about "Platinum 7s" is how its eleven prize levels are built. The prize money leans no one direction in particular. Games built like this offer both kinds of prizes without favoring either. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

The numbers for "Platinum 7s" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2422.headline: What type of game it is

2428.headline: A close look at the prizes

2429.body:
"MERRY MONEY TREE" is down to three top prizes after a $125,000 winner was claimed last week. The game started with four top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

If you play "MERRY MONEY TREE" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2429.headline: Fewer $125,000 prizes left

2430.body:
The top prize count on "WRAPPED IN RICHES" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has three of three top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "WRAPPED IN RICHES" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
